Fed cuts interest rates by a quarter point and signals more easing ahead

Published 2026-10-07 18:05 UTC

The Federal Reserve on Wednesday cut its key interest rate by a quarter percentage point, the third reduction this year, as policymakers grew more worried about a slowing labor market than about inflation.

The Federal Open Market Committee lowered the federal funds rate to a target range of 3.25%-3.5%. Two FOMC members dissented in favor of holding rates steady, a sign of division inside the central bank. The statement said downside risks to employment have risen.

At his news conference, Chair Jerome Powell said the Fed is well positioned to respond to incoming data and did not rule out another cut in December. Stocks rose after the decision, with the S&P 500 closing at a record, while Treasury yields fell.

Stocks rose after the decision, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.7% and the Nasdaq adding 1%. Treasury yields fell, with the 2-year yield, which is sensitive to Fed policy expectations, dropping to its lowest level in two years. The dollar weakened against major currencies.

Fed Chair remarks at the post-meeting press conference emphasized the cooling labor market. The chair said the committee sees the risks to employment as having increased and that policy is being adjusted to support the economy while keeping inflation on a path back to 2%. Futures markets now price in a high probability of another quarter-point cut in December.

The Fed's updated statement noted that job gains have slowed and that the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low. It described inflation as having eased over the past year while remaining somewhat elevated. Two officials dissented, reflecting division over how quickly to lower rates.

Economists said the decision was widely expected after recent weak payroll reports. The question now is how far the Fed will go. Some forecasters expect rates to fall below 3.5% next year, while others warn that sticky services inflation could limit the number of cuts. Mortgage rates have already dropped in anticipation, offering some relief to the housing market.

The Federal Reserve lowered interest rates for the third time this year as the jobs market cools, cutting the federal funds rate by a quarter point to a range of 3.75% to 4%. The unemployment rate has risen to its highest level in four years, and Fed officials signaled more easing ahead if hiring keeps slowing.
